column2: Seeing Rukmini united with her son, long lost, all the people in Dvaravati were then filled with wonder.

The form of all worlds, small and very subtle, is known by those who know all the Vedas and by none else; who is able to conquer him, the unborn, uncreated Lord, eternal, the primal benefactor of the world by his own will?
Thus addressed, she then resolved in her mind, "When?" and Parvati said to her again, "Who will be my husband?"
In Vaishakha, on the bright twelfth, whoever overcomes you in a dream, princess, will be your husband.
On that tithi, as the goddess had said, a man overcame her in a dream, and she conceived passion there; then, awakened, not seeing the man, eager,
shamelessly said to her friend "Where have you gone?", Brahmins. Bana's minister was Kumbhanda, and his daughter Chitralekha
was her friend; she said, "Who is this you speak of?" When Usha, overcome with shame, did not tell her,
then, gaining her trust, she told everything. When it was known, Usha said again what the goddess had said: "Find the means of getting him."
Then Chitralekha drew on a cloth the gods, Daityas and especially Gandharvas and humans and showed it.
Passing over Gandharvas, serpents, gods and Asuras, she turned her gaze to humans, and among them to the Andhakas and Vrishnis.
The fair-browed one, seeing Krishna and Rama, was bashful-eyed; seeing Pradyumna, Brahmins, she cast down her eyes in shame.
Seeing Aniruddha, then, shame was somehow cast away; saying "It is he, it is he, mine," the friend, going by yoga, went to Dvaravati, comforting Usha.
Bala also, with eyes closed, shared the torment produced by the touch of those ashes, through contact with Krishna's body.
Then, fighting with the Lord Sharngin, the Vaishnava fever was quickly expelled from Krishna's body.
Seeing it troubled and crushed by the blows of Narayana's arms, the god Grandfather said, "Let him be forgiven."
Then, saying "It is forgiven," the revered Madhusudana drew that Vaishnava fever back into himself.
Men who remember this battle of mine with you will be free of fever, said Hari, and went.
Then the revered Vishnu, having conquered the five fires and brought them to destruction, crushed in sport the Danava force.
Then Bali's son with the entire army of Daityas, Shankara and Karttikeya fought Shauri.
The battle between Hari and Shankara became very terrible; all the worlds were agitated, afflicted in many ways by weapons and missiles.
The gods thought that the dissolution of the whole world had surely come, while the great battle was going on.
With the jrimbhana weapon Govinda made Shankara yawn; then the Daityas and Pramathas fled on all sides.
Overcome by yawning, Hara sat down on the chariot-seat and could not then fight Krishna of untroubled deeds.
Guha, his arms wounded by Garuda and afflicted by Pradyumna's weapon, his power shaken by Krishna's roar, fled.
When Shankara was made to yawn, the Daitya army lost, Guha conquered and the host of Pramathas brought to destruction by the bow-bearer,
Bana, mounted on a great chariot with horses held by Nandisha, came there to fight Krishna and Krishna's son with his forces.
The very mighty Balabhadra pierced Bana's army in many ways; Pradyumna with arrows did not flee, out of dharma.
Bala was seen by Bana dragged by the plough-tip and crushed by the pestle, and Bana, with arrows, saw the discus-bearer.
Then a battle in brief took place between Krishna and Bana, with blazing weapons splitting each other's armour.
Krishna cut those arrows with an arrow shot by Bana; Bana pierced Keshava with arrows; the discus-bearer pierced Bana.
Bana and Krishna released weapons desiring victory, each intent on harming the other, and then clubs, Brahmins.
While all the weapons were being cut and the missile failed, Hari then set his mind on killing Bana at length.
Then Hari, destroyer of the Daitya hosts, took the discus Sudarshana, radiant with the brilliance of a hundred suns.
As the foe of Madhu released that discus to destroy Bana, a naked Daitya knowledge, Kotari, appeared before Hari.
Seeing her in front, Hari, closing his eyes, released Sudarshana at Bana to cut down the forest of the enemy's arms.
Impelled by Achyuta, it quickly cut Bana's arms one by one, by the throwing of weapons and missiles.
When the forest of arms was cut, Madhusudana, holding the discus in hand, wishing to kill Bana, was recognised by the foe of Tripura.
The lord of Uma sprang up and spoke to Govinda, conciliatory first, seeing Bana raining blood from the stumps of his arms:

Krishna, Krishna, lord of the world, I know you as Purushottama, the Supreme Lord, the Supreme Self, without beginning or end, the highest.
brahmapuran:206:42	This sport of yours, taking bodies among gods, animals and humans, this conduct, is marked by the slaying of Daityas.
brahmapuran:206:43	So be gracious: fearlessness has been given to this Bana by me, Lord; the word spoken by me must not be made untrue by you.
brahmapuran:206:44	This one who has grown through taking refuge in me has no offence against you, imperishable one; the Daitya was given a boon by me, so I ask your forgiveness.
Thus addressed, Govinda said to the trident-bearer, Uma's lord, with a gracious face, free of anger toward the Asura:

Let Bana live, Shankara, having a boon given by you; out of respect for your word I have turned back this discus.
brahmapuran:206:47	The fearlessness given by you is given by me; you ought to see yourself as not different from me, Shankara.
brahmapuran:206:48	What I am, you are, and this world with gods, Asuras and humans; people whose minds are deluded by ignorance see difference.
Having said so Krishna went to where Pradyumna's son (Aniruddha) was; the serpent bonds that bound him vanished, dried up by Garuda's wind.
Then, placing Aniruddha with his wife on Garuda, Rama, Pradyumna and Damodara came to Dvaraka city.
When this was said, the messenger gone, Hari, remembering, mounted Garuda and quickly went to that city.
Hearing of Keshava's undertaking, the lord of Kashi then came with the whole army as rear-guard.
Then Paundraka Vasudeva went toward Keshava with a great force and the Kashi king's force.
Hari saw him from afar standing in an excellent chariot, with discus, conch and mace in hand, holding a lotus in his hand,
wearing a garland, holding a Sharnga bow, with a banner bearing a Suparna design; Hari saw the Shrivatsa made on his chest,
wearing crown and earrings, in yellow garments. Seeing him, deep in feeling, Madhusudana laughed.
He fought with his army of elephants and horses, Brahmins, with swords, rishti lances, maces, spears, shaktis and bows.
In a moment, by arrows loosed from the Sharnga bow, fire-splitting, and by falls of mace and discus, he destroyed his force.
Having brought the Kashi king's force too to destruction, Janardana said to the foolish Paundraka, marked with his own emblems:

What was said by you, Paundraka, to me by the messenger's mouth, 'Give up the emblems' — I shall accomplish that for you.
brahmapuran:207:23	This discus is released; this mace of yours is let go; this Garuda is pointed out, let him mount your banner.
Saying so, he was split by the discus released, crushed by the mace, and Garuda (the banner bird) broken by Garuda.
Then, while the world cried alarm, the lord of the Kashis fought Vasudeva, standing for his friend's honour.
Then with arrows loosed from Sharnga he cut off his head and threw it into Kashi city, causing wonder in the world.
Having slain Paundraka and the Kashi king with followers, Shauri reached Dvaravati and played like an immortal gone to heaven.
Seeing that head fallen in the city of the Kashi king, the people, greatly amazed, asked, "What is this? By whom?"
Knowing that he had been killed by Vasudeva, his son, with the priest, then propitiated Shankara.
In the great field Avimukta, Shankara, pleased by him, said to the prince, "Choose a boon."
He chose: "Revered one, for my father's killer's death, let a Kritya (fierce spirit) rise against Krishna by your grace, Maheshvara."
Told "So it will be," right after the southern fire a great Kritya rose from that very fire-pit.
Then, with face fearsome with flames, flaming locks, angry, crying "Krishna, Krishna," she went to Dvaravati.
Seeing her terrible, with distorted eyes, all the people went to the refuge of the world, Madhusudana.
This great Kritya was produced by the Kashi king's son, who worshipped the bull-bannered Lord, to kill you, discus-bearer. Kill this fierce Kritya, her matted locks entangled with flames of fire.
The discus, set down while in sport he was engrossed in dice, matted with garlands of fire, terrible with the vomit of flames,
Vishnu's discus Sudarshana followed the Kritya at once. Then that Kritya, Maheshvari, struck by the discus,
went swiftly in haste; and the discus followed her; the Kritya, in haste, entered Varanasi itself,
her power struck by Vishnu's discus, best of sages. Then the great force of Kashi and the force of Pramathas,
equipped with all weapons and missiles, went to face the discus; having burned that force, abundant in discharge of weapons, with its brilliance,
the discus made the whole city of Varanasi unsafe, with abundant servants and citizens, with horses, elephants and people,
with all citadels and storehouses, unlookable even by the gods, its houses, walls and gates all enclosed by flames,
the discus burned that entire city quickly; its anger unabated, indifferent to whatever little means could achieve, that discus, flashing, returned to Vishnu's hand.
And all the kings, led by Bahlika, angry, said, seeing the Yadu line not worthy of a king, the pestle-armed (Balarama):

Ho, ho! What is this word spoken by you, Balabhadra? What Yadava will give commands to those born in the Kuru family?
brahmapuran:208:14	If Ugrasena too will give commands to the Kauravas, enough then of white umbrellas fit for kings and adorned.
brahmapuran:208:15	So go, Balabhadra; we shall not release Samba, of improper conduct, at your or Ugrasena's order.
brahmapuran:208:16	The bow made by the Kukuras and Andhakas to us, the honoured, was not made as a bow; what is this command from servant to master?
brahmapuran:208:17	You have been raised to pride by equal seats and food. What fault is yours, that policy pleases without regard?
brahmapuran:208:18	That which was offered to us by you as honour, Bala, was out of love only; it was not of our family but of the family suitable to you.
brahmapuran:208:19	Having said so, all the Kurus did not release Hari's son; having made one resolve, all entered Gajasahvaya (Hastinapura).
brahmapuran:208:20	Then Halayudha, intoxicated, swayed by anger born of the insult, rose and struck the ground with his heel.
brahmapuran:208:21	The earth was split by the great-souled one's heel-blow; he slapped his arm, filling the directions with the sound, and said, his eyes very red, his face crooked with a frown:
brahmapuran:208:22	Ah, the great arrogance of these wicked, worthless Kauravas; the sovereignty over us is surely time's.
Those who do not obey Ugrasena's command, or do not respect it — Shachi's lord would accept the command by dharma along with the gods.
Ugrasena always sits in the Sudharma hall of Shachi's lord; shame on their satisfaction with a throne left by hundreds of men.
He whose servants' women bear the clusters of flowers of the Parijata tree — he is not their lord of the earth.
Let Ugrasena, lord of all earth-kings, stay; today I shall make the earth without Kauravas and go to that city.
Karna, Duryodhana, Drona, Bhishma with Bahlika, Duhshasana and the rest, Bhuri and Bhurishravas,
Somadatta, Shala, Bhima, Arjuna with Yudhishthira, the twins and other Kauravas I shall kill, with horses, chariots and elephants.
Taking that hero Samba with his wife, I shall go to the city of Dvaraka and see my kin led by Ugrasena.
Or, together with all the Kurus, the Kauravas and the rest, urged quickly by the king of gods for the removal of the burden,
I shall throw the city of Nagasahvaya at once into the Bhagirathi."
Having said so, his eyes red with anger, palm-bannered, the pestle-armed one placed his plough, tip downward, on the rampart and dragged it.
Hastinapura then suddenly reeled; seeing it, all the Kauravas, their hearts agitated, cried out:

Rama, Rama, mighty-armed one! Forgive, forgive! Let your anger be withdrawn; be gracious, pestle-armed.
brahmapuran:208:35	Here is Samba with his wife, Bala, handed over to you; forgive the offenders who did not know your power.
Then the Kauravas, best of sages, came out of their city quickly and handed Samba over with his wife.
Bowing to Bhishma, Drona, Kripa and others, speaking pleasantly, Bala, best of the strong, said, "It is forgiven by me."
Even today that city is seen with a reeling form, Brahmins; this is the power of Rama, possessed of strength and valour.
Then the Kauravas, honouring Samba with Halin (Balarama), sent him off with marriage wealth and his wife.
And standing in the middle of the ocean he agitated the sea again; Brahmins, the sea, greatly agitated by him, overflows its shores,
flooding the villages and cities born on the shore with great speed, taking a form at will, a great form, ruining crops many times,
rolling in tumbling and crushing, the monkey crushed. By that evil-souled one this whole world was wronged,
without Vedic study or vashat, and the Brahmins were very distressed. Once in the Raivata garden Halayudha drank wine,
and Revati, the fortunate, and other excellent women too; sung to, he who moved amid the crest of playful women,
the best of Yadus, delighted like Kubera on Mandara. Then the monkey approached, took the plough of the Plough-bearer,
and the pestle and mocked him to his face, and the monkey also laughed at the women, facing them.
He threw and struck wine-filled jars; then, with mind filled with anger, he threatened Bala.
Yet disregarding him he made a screeching sound; then Bala rose and took up the pestle in anger.
The monkey, best of leapers, took up a terrible mountain rock and flung it; the best of Yadavas split it a thousandfold with the pestle,
and it fell on the ground. Leaping over the falling pestle, the monkey stretched with force and in rage struck him on the chest; then Bala, angry, struck him on the head with his fist.
Dvivida fell, vomiting blood, his life exhausted; by his falling body the mountain peak was shattered.
Sages, as if struck a hundredfold by Indra's thunderbolt; then the gods showered flowers on Rama,
and came and praised: "Well done, a great deed done by you. By this wicked monkey, helper of the Daitya side, the world was wronged; by good fortune he has met his end."
Such and many other immeasurable deeds of the wise Baladeva, Shesha, supporter of the earth.

For the removal of the earth's burden, for more than a hundred years the revered one has descended here, propitiated by the thirty gods.
brahmapuran:210:19	The wicked Daityas have been killed, the earth's burden has been lifted; with you as master let the thirty gods go to the lordship of heaven.
brahmapuran:210:20	That more than a hundred years have passed, lord of the world. Now, if it pleases you, you should go to heaven.
brahmapuran:210:21	The god, informed by the gods, said, 'Your delight is indeed here; therefore let it stay as the time is; the servants should be told.'
brahmapuran:210:22	What you have said, messenger, all that I know; and the destruction of the Yadavas has already been begun by me.
brahmapuran:210:23	This great burden of the earth, the Yadavas, not yet removed, I shall quickly bring to an end in seven nights.
brahmapuran:210:24	Having taken Dvaraka back from the ocean as it was taken, and withdrawn the Yadavas, I shall go to the abode of the thirty.
brahmapuran:210:25	Having abandoned the human body, with Sankarshana as companion, I shall have come; so should Devendra and the gods think.
brahmapuran:210:26	Jarasandha and others, the causes of the burden, have been slain; the earth's burden due to them was held by the Yadavas.
brahmapuran:210:27	So having removed this very great burden of the earth, I shall go for the protection of the world of the immortals; tell them.
Thus told by Vasudeva, the messenger of the gods bowed to him, Brahmins, and went by divine course to the king of gods.
The revered one then saw divine portents, earthly and aerial, day and night, in Dvaraka city, for destruction.
Seeing them he said to the Yadavas, "Behold these very terrible great portents; to appease them let us go to Prabhasa without delay."
The great devotee Uddhava bowed to Hari and said:
Revered one, whatever is to be done by me, command it now. I think the revered one will destroy this whole family; I perceive signs of this family's destruction, Achyuta.

Go by the divine course arisen from my grace to the holy hermitage Badari on Mount Gandhamadana,
brahmapuran:210:34	to the place of Nara-Narayana, on the earth made holy; with your mind on me, by my grace you will obtain success there.
brahmapuran:210:35	I shall go to heaven after withdrawing the family; and Dvaraka, abandoned by me, the sea will flood.
Thus told, Uddhava bowed to him and went to the place of Nara-Narayana, permitted by Keshava.
Then all those Yadavas mounted swift chariots and went to Prabhasa with Krishna, Rama and the rest, Brahmins.
Arrived at Prabhasa, pure and pleased, the Kukuras and Andhakas, permitted by Vasudeva, drank liquor there.
As they drank, from mutual collision among the Yadavas there arose a fire of quarrel, bringing destruction.
They struck one another with weapons, made so by the force of fate; when their weapons were exhausted, they took up the nearby eraka reeds.
The eraka reeds taken by them seemed to be like thunderbolts; with them they struck one another with very terrible blows.
Pradyumna, Samba and others, Kritavarman, Satyaki, Aniruddha and others, Prithu and Viprithu,
Charuvarman, Sucharu, Akrura and the rest, Brahmins, struck one another with thunderbolts in the form of eraka.
Hari tried to stop them, but the Yadavas thought Keshava had come to help them and struck one another.
